paper_title: Well-defined NHC–Pd(II)–Im(NHC=N-heterocyclic carbene; Im=1-methylimidazole) complex catalyzed C–N coupling of primary amines with aryl chlorides
mechanistic_insights: The reaction is highly sensitive to the base and solvent; KOtBu in toluene was found to be optimal, while other bases (LiOtBu, NaOtBu, NaOH, carbonates, phosphates) were ineffective.
Increasing the reaction temperature from 70 °C to refluxing toluene significantly improved the yield from 69% to 95%.

The NHC-Pd(II)-Im catalyst demonstrates high activity for sterically hindered substrates, successfully coupling ortho-substituted aryl chlorides with ortho-substituted primary anilines to form tetra-ortho-substituted diarylamines in excellent yields (84-99%).
When using primary alkyl amines (e.g., n-octylamine), bis-amination to form the tertiary amine is a significant competing reaction, often becoming the major product.
Steric hindrance on the aryl chloride can control selectivity in alkyl amine coupling; the reaction of 2,6-dimethylphenyl chloride with n-octylamine yielded only the mono-aminated product.

quantitative_outcomes.best_performing_conditions: Aryl chloride (0.8 mmol), primary amine (1.2 equiv), NHC-Pd(II)-Im catalyst 1 (1.0 mol%), KOtBu (1.0 mmol) in refluxing toluene (1.0 mL) for 4 hours.
quantitative_outcomes.notes: The catalytic system is highly efficient, providing good to high yields for a broad range of primary amines and aryl chlorides, including heteroaryl chlorides, within 4 hours. Its most notable feature is the exceptional performance with sterically demanding substrates, which are typically challenging for C-N coupling reactions.
